extra.message: The application removes and recreates the database file (vulns.db) on every startup. While not a direct security vulnerability, this causes data loss and could be used to trigger a denial of service by repeatedly causing restarts.

None of the API endpoints defined in swagger.yml (xssreflected, lfivuln, rfivuln, hhivuln, sstivuln, sqlivuln) have any authentication or authorization mechanisms. All routes are publicly accessible without any form of credential verification or session check.
The application binds to 0.0.0.0 (all network interfaces), making it accessible from any network interface rather than just localhost.

The Flask application is configured with debug=True on line 24. This enables the Werkzeug debugger which provides an interactive debug console in the browser. An attacker can achieve Remote Code Execution (RCE) through the debugger console.

The USERS table stores passwords as a plain VARCHAR column with no hashing or encryption. User records are inserted with cleartext passwords ('kaines', 'admin'). Anyone with database access (including via SQL injection) can read all users' passwords in plaintext.
The USERS table stores passwords in plaintext with no hashing whatsoever. Any SQL injection vulnerability or database access instantly exposes all user credentials.
The database setup inserts hardcoded user credentials 'mike' and 'kaines' into the USERS table in plaintext. These credentials are stored in source code and in the database without hashing.
Hardcoded user credentials (mike/kaines) are inserted directly into the database as plaintext, without quoting the string values (causing SQL syntax issues and exposing credentials in source code).
The hhivuln endpoint (which processes Host header injection) has no rate limiting. An attacker can send unlimited crafted requests to exploit the Host header injection vulnerability.
The /hhivuln POST endpoint has no authentication checks, allowing any unauthenticated attacker to exploit the Host Header injection vulnerability.

The `Host` HTTP header is read and reflected into the application's response without any validation. The Host header is used in constructing an HTML anchor tag, allowing an attacker to inject arbitrary content via a manipulated Host header.

The Host header value from the request is reflected directly into an HTML href attribute without any sanitization or escaping. The response constructs an HTML anchor tag with the Host header value, allowing an attacker to inject arbitrary HTML/JavaScript by sending a malicious Host header.
The lfivuln endpoint (which performs file reads based on user input) has no rate limiting. An attacker can send unlimited requests to read arbitrary files without restriction.
The /lfivuln POST endpoint has no authentication checks. Any unauthenticated user can exploit the path traversal vulnerability to read arbitrary files.

User-controlled `filename` parameter is passed directly to `open()` without any sanitization or path validation. An attacker can use path traversal sequences (`../../etc/passwd`) to read arbitrary files on the server.
User-controlled 'filename' parameter is passed directly to open() without any path sanitization or validation. An attacker can traverse directories to read arbitrary files.
The requests.get() call uses verify=False, which disables SSL/TLS certificate validation. This applies to any URL the SSRF endpoint fetches.

The `imagelink` parameter from user input is passed directly as a URL to `requests.get(url=name)`. An attacker can make the server send HTTP requests to arbitrary internal or external URLs, enabling Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF). Combined with verify=False, this is even more dangerous.

The rfivuln endpoint (which makes HTTP requests to user-supplied URLs) has no rate limiting. An attacker can send unlimited requests to probe internal networks or exploit the SSRF vulnerability without restriction.
The /rfivuln POST endpoint has no authentication. Any unauthenticated attacker can exploit the SSRF vulnerability to probe internal networks.
User-controlled 'imagelink' parameter is passed to requests.get() which fetches the URL server-side. No validation or allowlist is applied to the URL.

The sqlivuln endpoint (which accepts username/password and performs database queries) has no rate limiting or brute-force protection. An attacker can send unlimited requests to enumerate credentials or exploit the SQL injection.
The /sqlivuln POST endpoint (mapped to sqli.sqlivuln) has no authentication or authorization checks. Any unauthenticated user can access this endpoint and exploit the SQL injection vulnerability.
User-controlled 'username' parameter is concatenated directly into a SQL query using an f-string. No parameterization or escaping is used.

The raw database exception message (including SQL syntax errors) is returned to the user in the HTTP response. This exposes internal error details that can aid attackers in crafting SQL injection payloads.

The complete result of the SQL query (all user records) is returned directly in the HTTP response body. This includes username and password pairs for all matching users, exposing sensitive credential data.
The sstivuln endpoint (which performs Server-Side Template Injection) has no rate limiting. An attacker can send unlimited payloads to exploit the SSTI vulnerability without restriction.
The /sstivuln POST endpoint has no authentication, allowing any unauthenticated attacker to exploit the Server-Side Template Injection vulnerability.
User-controlled 'mathexp' parameter is concatenated directly into a Jinja2 Template object. Jinja2 templates support arbitrary Python expression evaluation, allowing remote code execution.

The mathexp parameter from user input is concatenated directly into a Jinja2 Template string and then rendered. This allows an attacker to inject arbitrary Jinja2 template expressions, enabling Server-Side Template Injection which can lead to Remote Code Execution.
The xssreflected POST endpoint (which reflects user input in the response) has no rate limiting. An attacker can send unlimited XSS payload probes without restriction.
The /xssreflected POST endpoint has no authentication, allowing any unauthenticated user to craft reflected XSS payloads.

The username parameter from user input is directly reflected in the JSON response without any HTML escaping or sanitization. If this response is rendered in a browser context (HTML page), it enables Cross-Site Scripting.
